chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Yusuf, from Sayf ibn ʿAmirah, from some of our companions, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
Between every two calls there is a sitting, except for al-Maghrib, for indeed between them there is only a breath.

key_terms.أَذَانَيْنِ: the two calls, meaning the adhan and the iqamah
key_terms.قَعْدَةٌ: a sitting or pause between the two calls
key_terms.نَفَسًا: a breath, meaning a very short interval

ai.seo_question: Is there a recommended sitting between the adhan and iqamah in Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states a ruling about sitting between the adhan and iqamah for the prayers. It indicates that a pause is observed between the two calls in general, except in Maghrib, where the interval is very brief.
